harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a "Fleet Internal CA" root CA on node1, issued a node2 TLS server certificate (CN=node2, SANs DNS:node2/IP:10.100.159.11) signed by that CA, deployed the cert+key to node2 and configured nginx to serve HTTPS on port 8443 with it, and installed the CA into the system trust store (update-ca-certificates) on both node1 and node2. Verified end-to-end trust (curl with no --cacert override returns "SSL certificate verify ok" / HTTP 200) from both nodes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1 then node2, confirming boot_id changes and full post-restart recovery of nginx/TLS/CA trust on both nodes.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/tooling on node1 and node2 (Ubuntu 24.04, openssl, python3 present; no nginx initially)
Installed nginx on node2 via apt to serve HTTPS
Generated 4096-bit CA key and self-signed 'Fleet Internal CA' root cert on node1 (/root/fleet-ca)
Generated node2 key + CSR with SAN (DNS:node2, IP:10.100.159.11) and signed it with the CA (825-day cert)
Transferred ca.crt, node2.crt, node2.key from node1 to node2 via a temporary python3 http.server (SSH unavailable, no sshd running on node2), then tore down the transfer server and removed temp files

Configured nginx on node2 (/etc/nginx/sites-available/fleet-tls.conf) to listen on 8443 with ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key pointing at the issued cert/key; validated config and enabled+started nginx
Verified TLS handshake, SAN match, and cert chain from both node1 and node2 using --cacert against the new CA
Installed the CA cert into /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and ran update-ca-certificates on both node1 and node2
Re-verified HTTPS trust works via system trust store alone (no explicit --cacert) on both nodes, receiving 'SSL certificate verify ok' and HTTP 200
Captured baseline boot_id/uptime and service health on both nodes
Restarted node1 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified CA files/trust store and cross-node HTTPS still worked
Restarted node2 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified nginx auto-started, port 8443 listening, and HTTPS/CA trust fully recovered
Final cross-check from node1 confirming HTTP 200 and 'SSL certificate verify ok' against node2 post-restart

evidence.requirement: Create CA 'Fleet Internal CA' on node1
evidence.summary: openssl generated CA key and self-signed cert; subject/dates confirm CN=Fleet Internal CA, O=Fleet Internal CA, valid 2026-2036

evidence.requirement: Issue TLS certificate for node2 signed by the CA
evidence.summary: CSR generated and signed by ca.crt/ca.key; resulting cert shows subject=CN=node2, issuer=Fleet Internal CA, SAN DNS:node2/IP:10.100.159.11

evidence.requirement: Deploy cert/key to node2 and configure HTTPS on port 8443
evidence.summary: Cert/key copied to /etc/ssl/fleet on node2; nginx config validated (nginx -t); nginx active and listening on 0.0.0.0:8443/[::]:8443; curl over HTTPS with CA trust returns served content

evidence.requirement: Certificate served correctly over TLS (SAN/issuer match, chain trusted)
evidence.summary: curl -v from node2 and node1 respectively show TLS1.3 handshake, subject=CN=node2, SAN IP match, issuer=Fleet Internal CA

evidence.requirement: Install CA as trusted system CA on both node1 and node2
evidence.summary: update-ca-certificates run on both nodes, each reporting '1 added, 0 removed; done' after copying ca.crt to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates

evidence.requirement: Prove system trust store (not just explicit --cacert) trusts the CA
evidence.summary: curl without --cacert from both node1 and node2 to https://10.100.159.11:8443 returns 'SSL certificate verify ok' and HTTP 200

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 1e0cb179... and uptime start 20:15:28 prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot command acknowledged (pid returned) before disconnect

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: uptime -s now shows 20:17:02 (new boot) and boot_id changed to 48142d03..., distinct from pre-restart 1e0cb179...

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of CA data and trust
evidence.summary: CA files intact under /root/fleet-ca, fleet-internal-ca.pem present in trust store, and cross-node HTTPS to node2 returns HTTP 200 after node1 reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 901ef286..., uptime start 20:15:28, nginx active, and successful HTTPS content fetch prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot command acknowledged (pid returned) before disconnect

evidence.requirement: node2 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Connection timed out during reboot window, then reachable again with new uptime start 20:17:17 and boot_id changed to a579bf39..., distinct from pre-restart 901ef286...

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of TLS service, CA trust, and cluster reachability
evidence.summary: nginx auto-active, port 8443 listening again, fleet-internal-ca.pem still in trust store, HTTPS returns 200, and node1 confirms full cert chain verify ok against node2 post-restart
